title: State and cascading values
summary: CascadingValue, state containers, and persisting prerendered state.

predict.title: Matched by type
options: **Theme: Dark**
**Theme:** with nothing after it
An error: no cascading value of type `string`
**Theme: Theme**
predict.explanation: A `[CascadingParameter]` is matched **by type**, not by property name. The layout cascades a `Theme`, but the component asks for a `string`, so nothing matches. The property stays `null` and Blazor reports **no error**. Ask for `public Theme? Theme { get; set; }` and render `@Theme?.Name`.

predict.title: Across the island
predict.body:
The app has **no global render mode**, so the layout is static SSR. MainLayout.razor: ```razor @Body ``` The page is static too, and contains one interactive component: ```razor ``` ThemeLabel.razor: ```razor

@(Theme is null ? "No theme" : Theme.Name)

@code { [CascadingParameter] public Theme? Theme { get; set; } } ``` **Once `ThemeLabel` is interactive, what does it show?**
options: The theme's name, like in any other component
**No theme**
An error: `Theme` is not serializable
Nothing: the component doesn't render at all
predict.explanation: An interactive component inside a static page is an **island**: it runs in its own, separate tree. A `<CascadingValue>` in the static layout does **not** cross that render mode boundary, so `Theme` is `null`. Fix it with a root-level value (`builder.Services.AddCascadingValue(...)`) or by making the whole app interactive.

predict.title: The count that doesn't move
options: **Cart: 1**
**Cart: 0**
An error: `OnChange` has no subscribers
**Cart: 1**, but only after a page refresh
predict.explanation: The item **is** added to the service, but `CartCount` never subscribed to `OnChange`, so nobody tells it to re-render. Only `ProductCard` re-renders (it handled the click). `CartCount` keeps showing **0** until it re-renders for another reason. A refresh would make it worse: on Server it starts a new circuit with an empty cart. Subscribe in `OnInitialized` and call `InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged)`.

predict.title: How many fetches?
options: Once
Twice
Three times
Zero: `OnInitializedAsync` doesn't run during prerendering
predict.explanation: **Twice.** The component runs once to **prerender** the HTML, then a new instance runs again when the circuit starts and it becomes interactive. Both runs call `OnInitializedAsync`, so the data is fetched twice. Persist it with `[PersistentState]` (or `PersistentComponentState`) to fetch it only once.

practice.title: Read a cascading value
practice.task:
The layout already cascades a `Theme` object:

```razor
<CascadingValue Value="theme">@Body</CascadingValue>
```

Right now every page has to pass `Theme="@theme"` to `ThemedButton`. Change the button so it **receives the theme as a cascading parameter** instead. Keep the name `Theme`, and make it nullable, because it may be missing.
practice.hint: A cascading parameter looks like a parameter, with a different attribute: `[CascadingParameter]`.

checks.label: A `[CascadingParameter] public Theme? Theme` property
checks.hint: Write `[CascadingParameter] public Theme? Theme { get; set; }`.

practice.title: Provide a fixed value
practice.task:
Make the layout give `theme` to **every page** below it:

1. Wrap `@Body` in a **`<CascadingValue>`** whose `Value` is `theme`.
2. The theme never changes while the app runs, so tell Blazor with **`IsFixed="true"`**.

practice.title: A state container
practice.task:
Finish **`CartState`**, a service that several components share:

1. Add a public event **`OnChange`** of type `Action?`.
2. Add a private method **`NotifyStateChanged`** that raises it (only if someone subscribed).
3. Make **`Add`** call `NotifyStateChanged()` after adding the item.

(It is registered with `builder.Services.AddScoped<CartState>();`.)
practice.hint: `public event Action? OnChange;` and `private void NotifyStateChanged() => OnChange?.Invoke();`

practice.title: Subscribe and unsubscribe
practice.task:
`CartCount` shows the number of items, but it doesn't update when another component adds one. Fix it:

1. In **`OnInitialized`**, subscribe a method **`OnCartChanged`** to `Cart.OnChange`.
2. `OnCartChanged` re-renders with **`InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged)`**.
3. Implement **`IDisposable`** and unsubscribe in **`Dispose`**.
practice.hint: Use `+=` in `OnInitialized` and `-=` in `Dispose`, with the same method.

practice.title: Stop the double fetch with [PersistentState]
practice.task:
This page is prerendered, so `GetAllAsync` runs twice. Use the **.NET 10** way to fetch only once:

1. Replace the field with a **public property** `Products` (type `List<Product>?`) marked **`[PersistentState]`**.
2. In `OnInitializedAsync`, fetch only if nothing was restored, with **`??=`**.
3. Update the markup to use `Products`.
practice.hint: `[PersistentState] public List<Product>? Products { get; set; }` and `Products ??= await ...;`

checks.label: A `[PersistentState] public List<Product>? Products` property
checks.hint: Write `[PersistentState] public List<Product>? Products { get; set; }`. It must be public.

checks.label: The old private field is gone

practice.title: Persist state by hand, from scratch
practice.task:
Fix the double fetch on this page with the older **`PersistentComponentState`** API (you will see it in a lot of AI code):

1. Inject **`PersistentComponentState`** as `AppState`, and implement **`IDisposable`**.
2. In `OnInitializedAsync`, register a callback with **`RegisterOnPersisting`** and keep the subscription in a field.
3. Use **`TryTakeFromJson<WeatherForecast[]>("forecasts", ...)`**. Only call the service when it returns `false`.
4. The callback saves `forecasts` with **`PersistAsJson("forecasts", ...)`**.
5. Dispose the subscription in **`Dispose`**.
practice.hint: Look at the `PersistentComponentState` example at the end of the theory, and use the key `"forecasts"` in both places.

checks.label: Keeps the result of `AppState.RegisterOnPersisting(...)` in a field
checks.hint: Write `subscription = AppState.RegisterOnPersisting(Persist);` with a `PersistingComponentStateSubscription subscription;` field.

quiz.body: A component has `[CascadingParameter] public Theme? Theme { get; set; }` with no `Name`. How does Blazor find its value?
options: By the property name: an ancestor must cascade a value called `Theme`
From the DI container, like `@inject`
By type: the closest ancestor that cascades a `Theme` value
The parent must pass it as an attribute: `Theme="@theme"`
quiz.explanation: Without `Name`, a cascading parameter is matched **by type**, and the **closest** ancestor `<CascadingValue>` of that type wins. If nothing matches, the property is `null`, with no error.

options: It says the value never changes, so Blazor doesn't track the components that use it
It makes the value read-only for the components that receive it
It keeps the value when the user refreshes the page
It makes the value cross render mode boundaries
quiz.explanation: `IsFixed` is a **performance** hint: the value won't change, so Blazor skips tracking subscribers. If the value does change later, the components that use it are not updated.

quiz.body: You want a `Theme` cascading value for the **whole app**, set up once in `Program.cs`. Which line does that?
options: `builder.Services.AddScoped<CascadingValue<Theme>>();`
`app.UseCascadingValue(new Theme());`
`builder.Services.AddSingleton<Theme>();` plus `[CascadingParameter]`
`builder.Services.AddCascadingValue(sp => new Theme());`
quiz.explanation: `AddCascadingValue` registers a **root-level** cascading value. Components read it with `[CascadingParameter]`, as if a `<CascadingValue>` wrapped the whole app. A plain `AddSingleton` is a service: you would read it with `@inject`, not `[CascadingParameter]`.

quiz.body:
A static SSR page renders `

Hi

`. It throws. Why?
options: `Dialog` must be in the `.Client` project

`

Hi

` is a `RenderFragment` (`ChildContent`), which can't be serialized and passed into an interactive component
Interactive components can't have child content at all
`@rendermode` can't be used on a component tag
quiz.explanation: Parameters passed from a static parent into an interactive island must be **serializable**. A `RenderFragment` is code, not data, so Blazor refuses it. Cascading values from the static parent don't cross the boundary either.

quiz.body: On Blazor Server, a `CartState` service must hold **one cart per user**. Which lifetime fits?
options: Singleton
Scoped
Transient
Any lifetime: Blazor makes state per user automatically
quiz.explanation: On Interactive Server, **Scoped** means one instance per **circuit** (one per user tab). A Singleton would share one cart between all users. Transient would give each component its own cart, so nothing is shared.

quiz.body: Why does a component call `InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged)` in its `OnChange` handler, instead of just `StateHasChanged()`?
options: `StateHasChanged()` only works inside `OnAfterRender`
`InvokeAsync` saves the state to the browser first
It is the same thing; `InvokeAsync` is only for style
The event can be raised from another component or a background task, and `InvokeAsync` runs the re-render on this component's own dispatcher
quiz.explanation: The handler runs on whatever code raised the event: another component's click, or a timer thread. `InvokeAsync` moves the call onto **this** component's dispatcher. Calling `StateHasChanged()` from the wrong context can throw.

quiz.body: A user on an **Interactive Server** app presses F5 (refresh). What happens to the data in their scoped services and component fields?
options: It is lost: the old circuit ends and a new one starts with new instances
It is kept, because scoped services live on the server
It is kept, because Blazor saves it in the browser automatically
It is kept only if the component uses `IsFixed`
quiz.explanation: A refresh starts a **new circuit**, so every scoped service and component is created again. To survive a refresh, keep the data in browser storage (like `ProtectedSessionStorage`) or on the server (a database).

quiz.body: A prerendered component calls `await ProtectedLocalStorage.GetAsync<int>("count")` in `OnInitializedAsync` and fails during prerendering. What is the fix?
options: Register `ProtectedLocalStorage` as a singleton
Use `[PersistentState]` on the storage service
Move the call to `OnAfterRenderAsync` (on `firstRender`), because JS interop isn't available during prerendering
Use `IsFixed="true"`
quiz.explanation: Protected browser storage uses **JS interop**, and there is no browser connection while the server prerenders. Read it in `OnAfterRenderAsync(firstRender)`, then call `StateHasChanged()`.

quiz.body: In the `PersistentComponentState` pattern, when does `TryTakeFromJson<T>("key", out var value)` return `true`?
options: On every render, after the first one
Only when the user has visited the page before
When the key exists in `localStorage`
When the interactive run finds a value that the prerender saved with `PersistAsJson`
quiz.explanation: During prerendering, the `RegisterOnPersisting` callback saves values with `PersistAsJson`. They are written into the HTML. On the interactive run, `TryTakeFromJson` finds them and returns `true`, so you skip the second fetch.

quiz.body: Which use of the .NET 10 `[PersistentState]` attribute is correct?
options: `[PersistentState] public List<Order>? Orders { get; set; }` and `Orders ??= await Service.GetAsync();` in `OnInitializedAsync`
`[PersistentState] private List<Order>? orders;` and `orders = await Service.GetAsync();`
`[PersistentState]` on the `@inject` line of the service
`[PersistentState]` on the `OnInitializedAsync` method
quiz.explanation: `[PersistentState]` goes on a **public property**. Blazor restores it before `OnInitializedAsync` on the interactive run, so `??=` fetches only when nothing was restored.

interview.question: What is a cascading value in Blazor?
interview.modelAnswer: A value that a component provides to **all** its descendants, at any depth, with `<CascadingValue>`. Descendants receive it with `[CascadingParameter]`, matched by type (or by `Name`). It avoids passing the same parameter through every level, and is often used for themes, the current user, or auth state.

interview.question: What is the difference between `[Parameter]` and `[CascadingParameter]`?
interview.modelAnswer: A `[Parameter]` is set explicitly by the direct parent, as an attribute. A `[CascadingParameter]` is supplied by any ancestor's `<CascadingValue>` (or a root-level value), matched by type or name, without the parent writing anything. If no cascading value matches, it is simply `null`.

interview.question: What do `Name` and `IsFixed` do on `<CascadingValue>`?
interview.modelAnswer: `Name` lets a consumer pick the value by name with `[CascadingParameter(Name = "...")]`, which you need when two values have the same type. `IsFixed="true"` says the value never changes, so Blazor doesn't track subscribers. It is a performance optimization.

interview.question: What is a root-level cascading value?
interview.modelAnswer: A cascading value registered in `Program.cs` with `builder.Services.AddCascadingValue(...)`. It is available to the whole app without a `<CascadingValue>` in the layout, including interactive components that run in a separate tree. `AddCascadingAuthenticationState()` is a common example.

interview.question: Why doesn't a cascading value from a static layout reach an interactive component?
interview.modelAnswer: Because an interactive island in a static page runs in its own component tree, so there is no ancestor `<CascadingValue>` there. Parameters into an island must also be serializable, so a `RenderFragment` can't cross. Use a root-level cascading value or make the whole app interactive.

interview.question: Describe the state container pattern.
interview.modelAnswer: A plain class registered as a scoped service that holds shared state and exposes an `event Action? OnChange`. Methods that change the state call `NotifyStateChanged()`, which raises the event. Components inject it, subscribe in `OnInitialized`, call `InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged)` in the handler, and unsubscribe in `Dispose`.

interview.question: Where can state be lost in a Blazor app?
interview.modelAnswer: Component fields are lost when the component is disposed, for example on navigation. On Interactive Server, the circuit (scoped services) is lost on refresh, closing the tab, or a failed reconnect. On WebAssembly, all memory is lost on refresh. To keep state, use browser storage (`ProtectedLocalStorage`/`ProtectedSessionStorage` on Server, `localStorage` via JS on WebAssembly) or a database.

interview.question: What is the double fetch problem, and how do you fix it?
interview.modelAnswer: With prerendering, a component runs twice: once on the server to produce HTML and again when it becomes interactive, so `OnInitializedAsync` loads the data twice and the UI can flicker. Fix it by persisting the prerendered data into the page: in .NET 10 with `[PersistentState]` on a public property and `??=`, or with `PersistentComponentState` (`RegisterOnPersisting`, `PersistAsJson`, `TryTakeFromJson`).
